correctness.rationale: For 0<a<1, b>1, a(b+1)>1, check c=(1+a)b+a, mu=a/(1+a), q=1/(1+a), U=c/(1+a). Initial risk-zero points x<=q take exactly two steps; x>q take one. Lower intermediate tentative second risk is -(1+c)x, which has absolute value>1 because ac>1 follows from a(b+1)>1. All signed return points flip sign, with absolute factors c and a. The two return branches partition [mu,U] in their images, and dx/x is preserved. The suspension probability is normalized by K=log c+2log(1/a), invariant by exact change of variables, and has zero atom H/K plus signed 1/(2K|s|) density on a<|s|<1. The inverse parameter formulas follow algebraically. Irrational return ratio gives ergodicity of the sign-flipping extension and the full-time ergodic theorem. Exact-rational checks, quadrature, and 150000-step trajectory checks support the proof but are not its basis. The original-time reset count has exact return epochs tau_m=2m-floor(u_0+m h/H)=mK/H+u_m-u_0, and intervening stages yield |Z_n-n H/K|<1 for every n with no irrationality requirement.

value.rationale: The studied risk-reset map is a motivated hysteretic dynamical model. A scalar risk trace is a natural observable, and the difference between one-step and two-step physical visits changes its actual-time distribution. The theorem explicitly gives the reset-event frequency, full signed nonzero-risk distribution and sharp moment formulas, and establishes injective two-parameter recovery from the stationary marginal alone. These are quantitative and operational properties not supplied by the prior qualitative rotation and existence results. This is a natural exact invariant with potential use for data-based parameter identification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical recomputation. The strict unit discrepancy at every finite original-time horizon is an unusually strong deterministic constraint on observable resets, valid even for rational return rotations; it is not just an asymptotic law.
